intervals.note: Start 2023-11 is the first month of the reactor-on data set analysed in arXiv:2501.05206; the same paper says only that the setup moved to Leibstadt "In 2023", so actual operation may have begun earlier. Ongoing as of the most recent sourced publication (2601... i.e. May 2026 'New constraints on physics ... from the latest CONUS datasets', arXiv:2605.22815, referenced but not separately fetched/cited as a source in this pass).
intervals.quote: The data set used in the analysis reported here includes reactor on periods between November 2023 and July 2024 (327 kg d)

name: CONUS / CONUS+ HPGe detector array
notes: One detector record covers both phases: the CONUS+ overview paper (arXiv:2407.11912) states the CEvNS signature 'will be measured with the same four point-contact high-purity germanium (HPGe) detectors produced for the former experiment, however refurbished'.

placements.quote: positioned at 17.1m from the 3.9GWth reactor core of the nuclear power plant in Brokdorf, Germany
installed in the nuclear power plant in Leibstadt, Switzerland, at a distance of 20.7 m from the 3.6 GW thermal power reactor core

target_mass.display: 4 kg (4 x 1 kg) nominal; 2.83 +/- 0.02 kg active at Leibstadt
target_mass.note: Nominal array is four 1 kg point-contact HPGe detectors, reused at both sites. At Leibstadt only three of the four refurbished detectors were used in the Nov 2023-Jul 2024 analysis, giving an active mass of 2.83+/-0.02 kg; value/unit below record the original 4-detector nominal array mass.

summary.plain: Four one-kilogram blocks of ultra-pure germanium, first used at a German nuclear plant and later moved to a Swiss one, sensitive enough to feel the tiny nudge of a reactor antineutrino bouncing off a whole atomic nucleus.
summary.technical: Array of four 1 kg point-contact high-purity germanium (HPGe) spectrometers with sub-300 eV ionization thresholds; operated at Brokdorf (2018-2023, 17.1 m from a 3.9 GWth reactor core) and, refurbished, at Leibstadt from November 2023 (20.7 m from a 3.6 GWth reactor core; 2.83 kg active mass from 3 of 4 detectors in the first CONUS+ analysis).

technology.quote: coherent elastic scattering of electron antineutrinos emitted from a nuclear reactor off germanium nuclei
